## About the Foret Lab

The Foret Lab is an academic research group studying the structure, function,
and resilience of natural systems. Founded on the principles of open science and
collaborative inquiry, we develop and apply quantitative methods to questions
that matter for both science and society.

### Our approach

- **Reproducible research.** All of our analyses are built on open data and
  open-source tools, so that our results can be verified and extended by others.
- **Interdisciplinary collaboration.** We work across ecology, statistics, and
  computer science, partnering with researchers and practitioners worldwide.
- **Mentorship.** Training the next generation of scientists is central to our
  mission. We support students at every stage, from undergraduates to postdocs.

### Where we work

The lab is based within the Department of Environmental Science. Our fieldwork
spans temperate and boreal forest sites, while our computational work happens
both on campus and through high-performance computing collaborations.

### Funding & acknowledgements

Our research is supported by competitive grants from national science agencies
and private foundations. We are grateful to our funders, collaborators, and the
communities that host our field sites.
